CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  2175 Cherry Avenue • Signal Hill, California 90755-3799

  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL
  WELCOMES YOU TO A REGULAR
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  October 24, 2023

Meetings begin at 6:00 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in
closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with
the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment
on closed session matters at 6:00 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no
business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm.
There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting. Any person
wishing to comment shall be allotted three minutes per distinct item. Any meeting may be
adjourned to a time and place stated in the order of adjournment.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting on the City’s website and outside of City
Hall. The agenda and related reports are also available for review online at
www.cityofsignalhill.org.

To view or listen to the meeting live at 7:00 p.m.:

  • City of Signal Hill website at www.cityofsignalhill.org, select the City Council
  Meetings Link from the home page.
  • Charter Spectrum Channel 3 or Frontier FiOS Channel 38.
To view and participate (closed session at 6:00 p.m. and regular meeting at 7:00 p.m.):

  • In-person Participation: Council Chambers of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal
  Hill, California.
  • To make a general public comment or comment on a specific agenda item, you may
  also submit your comment, limited to 250 words or less, to the City Clerk at
  cityclerk@cityofsignalhill.org not later than 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday,October 24, 2023.
  Written comments will be provided electronically to City Council and attached to the
  meeting minutes. Written comments will not be read into the record.
City Council Members are compensated $722.18 per month. City Clerk and City Treasurer are
compensated $438.22 per month.

(12)  ORDINANCES

  a.  INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE TO REDESIGN THE CITY SEAL

  Summary:

  The City of Signal Hill was incorporated in April 1924. To recognize the City’s
  upcoming centennial milestone, the City Council formed the Centennial
  Celebration Committee (Committee) in January 2022.  The Committee
  collectively desired to propose a redesign of the current City seal. As such, staff
  is proposing a redesigned City seal for City Council consideration and
  introduction of an Ordinance to effectuate the adoption of the new City seal as
  required by the Signal Hill Municipal Code (SHMC).

  Recommendations:

  1.) Review and approve the redesigned proposed City Seal; and,

  2.) Introduce an ordinance, entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL
  HILL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING SECTION 1.02.010 AND SECTION
  1.02.020 OF CHAPTER 1.02 OF THE SIGNAL HILL MUNICIPAL CODE
  RELATING TO THE CITY SEAL.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.

  Page 3 of 7
 City Council  Regular  October 24, 2023

(13)  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

CALL THE CITY COUNCIL AS SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

  a.  RESOLUTIONS AMENDING THE CITY’S INVESTMENT POLICY

  Summary:

  The City Council, also acting as the City Council as Successor Agency
  (Successor Agency), will consider amending the City’s Investment Policy to
  provide greater diversification of the City’s investment portfolio and update the
  policy to conform to recent legislative changes. To provide greater investment
  diversification, City Council will consider approving a resolution authorizing the
  City of Signal Hill to join with other public agencies as a Shareholder of the
  California Asset Management Trust, a joint powers authority (JPA), to invest in
  shares of the Trust also known as California Asset Management Program
  (CAMP). Shareholders may choose to join as an Investor or a Participant; both
  receive the same investment results, but only Participants are members of the
  JPA. The City Council will also consider authorizing an update to the investment
  policy language due to recent legislative changes. In addition, the City Council
  as Successor Agency will consider amending a companion policy addressing
  Successor Agency funds.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.
  Recommendations:

  A. City Council to adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING ITS INVESTMENT POLICY FOR PUBLIC
  FUNDS

  B. Successor Agency to adopt a resolution, entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL AS SUCCESSOR AGENCY OF
  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING ITS INVESTMENT
  POLICY FOR PUBLIC FUNDS

  C. Approve the authorization to allow the City of Signal Hill to join as a
  participating shareholder of the California Asset Management Trust, a joint
  powers authority, to invest in shares of the Trust also known as CAMP.
RECESS THE CITY COUNCIL AS SUCCESSOR AGENCY

(14)  CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following Consent Calendar items are expected to be routine and
  non-controversial. Items will be acted upon by the Council at one time without
  discussion. Any item may be removed by a Council Member for discussion.
  a.  PROFESSIONAL CONSULTANT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH BUREAU
  VERITAS TECHNICAL ASSESSMENTS LLC FOR THE PREPARATION OF A
  FACILITIES MASTER PLAN

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider authorizing the City Manager to enter into a
  Professional Consultant Services Agreement with Bureau Veritas Technical
  Assessments LLC (BVTA) to prepare the City’s first Facilities Master Plan (FMP)
  for a cost of $50,937.05; authorize the Public Works Director to approve a term
  extension of up to 6 months; and utilize contingency of $25,000 for the
  preparation of updated as-built facility system drawings. The FMP aims to
  conduct a thorough evaluation of the City’s facilities and develop a concise set
  of objectives, policies, and routine maintenance schedules across all City
  facilities. The goal is to ensure the longevity and optimal condition of City
  facilities, including mechanical and electrical systems. This proposed plan would
  assist the Public Works Building Maintenance Division with identifying and
  prioritizing major repairs necessary to maintain City facilities at a desired service
  level. If approved by City Council, the work would begin in November 2023 and
  be completed by May 2024.

  Strategic Goal(s):

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure:  Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to enter into a Professional Consultant
  Services agreement with BVTA for the preparation of the Facilities Master
  Plan, for a term of six-months and a not-to-exceed contract amount of
  $50,937.05, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  2. Authorize the Public Works Director to utilize a project contingency of
  $25,000 and approve up to a 90-calendar day term extension, for the
  preparation of updated as-built drawings of all system components for
  each facility.
  b.  AMENDMENT TO MASTER AGREEMENT WITH WELLS FARGO BANK, N.A.
  FOR TREASURY MANAGEMENT SERVICES

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider entering into an amended Master Agreement with
  Page 5 of 7

  Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. (Wells Fargo) for the City’s treasury management
  services with an expiration date of October 2, 2028 to lock in lower service fee
  pricing through the stated term.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to enter into an amended Master
  Agreement with Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. for treasury management services and
  related fees, retroactive to October 1, 2023, and expiring on October 2, 2028, in
  a form approved by the City Attorney.
  c.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS AND MONTHLY TRANSACTION REPORT

  Summary:

  The Schedule of Investments is a listing of all surplus funds invested for both the
  City and the Successor Agency to the former Signal Hill Redevelopment Agency
  as of the date shown on the report. The monthly transaction report provides the
  changes in investments for the prior month.

  Strategic Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.
  Recommendation:

  Receive and file.
  d.  WARRANT REGISTER DATED OCTOBER 24, 2023

  Summary:

  The Warrant Register is a listing of all general disbursements issued since the

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.
  Recommendation:

  Authorize payment of the Warrant Register dated October 24, 2023.

  Tonight’s meeting will be adjourned to the next regular meeting of the Signal Hill City

CITIZEN PARTICIPATION

  Routine matters are handled most quickly and efficiently if contact is made with the City
  department directly concerned. However, if you would like to request that a matter be
  presented for City Council consideration, you may do so by writing to the City Council,
  City Clerk, or City Manager. The deadline for agenda items is 12 noon on the Tuesday
  preceding the Council and Agency meetings. The complete agenda, including back up
  materials is available on the City website on the Friday preceding the meeting.

  If you need special assistance beyond what is normally provided to participate in City
  meetings, the City will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner.
  Please call the City Clerk's office at (562) 989-7305 at least 48 hours prior to the
  meeting to inform us of your particular needs and to determine if accommodation is
  feasible.
